signals.title: USD/JPY — BoJ Policy Shift + Intervention Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 160.19, holding above the 160.00 psychological level which historically triggers Ministry of Finance verbal warnings and intervention risk. BoJ Governor Ueda confirms the bank will assess a September rate increase, noting that data since July matches projections while highlighting the impact of the Middle East conflict on FX policy guidance. Despite the hawkish pivot, the 270bp Fed-BoJ OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.68% vs TONA 0.98%) continues to support the pair. Options markets show significant concern regarding a sharp reversal, with 25d Risk Reversals at -1.79 indicating a strong put skew for downside protection. The pair remains above its SMA20 at 159.12, but the 160.00 breach invites policy-forced repricing. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish USD/JPY; intervention risk at 160.00+ overrides carry while VIX remains at 16.3. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: MoF remains sidelined at 160.00, allowing carry-seekers to extend the trend toward 162.00.

signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme
signals.text: NZD/USD is currently the primary G10 bilateral theme as the pair tests 0.5895, sitting below the SMA20 at 0.5912. The USD leads G10 performance with a +0.661% weekly average, while NZD lags at -0.504%, creating a 1.165% spread. Speculative positioning in NZD is at an extreme 0 percentile (pctl 52w) with a lev_net of -32,496, signaling a heavily crowded short. This positioning contradicts the RBNZ's hawkish market bias and a mildly restrictive +0.16% real policy rate. Any hawkish delivery at the upcoming meeting risks a disorderly short-squeeze in the laggard currency. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD; contrarian setup against crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: RBNZ holds and signals a neutral shift, validating the crowded spec short and extending NZD underperformance.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7149 is showing signs of late-trend exhaustion despite holding above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7114/0.7024/0.6978). COT speculative positioning is crowded long at a 95th percentile (z +1.92), yet retail sentiment has moved to an extreme 84% short. This divergence indicates retail traders are aggressively fading the institutional trend, which often precedes a final volatility spike or capitulation. While the 67bp OIS carry advantage favors AUD (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.68%), the negative real rate of -0.55% suggests the RBA's stance is less restrictive than peers. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; supported by carry and retail fading the trend. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold bias. Risk: A break below SMA20 at 0.7114 triggers a liquidation of the crowded institutional long.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3515, currently positioned below its SMA20 (1.3549) but above its SMA50/200 cluster near 1.3440. The options market is pricing in significant tail-risk with an Implied Volatility (IV) of 11.0% against a 30-day realized volatility (HV30) of only 4.8%. This results in a massive +6.2% Volatility Risk Premium (VRP), the highest in the G10 space, indicating high demand for GBP protection despite a neutral OIS carry differential against the USD. Speculative positioning is already crowded long (pctl 96, z +1.58), suggesting the market is paying up for downside hedges. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; high vol premium makes directional bets expensive. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep — hold bias. Risk: Realized volatility catches up to IV on a breakout below the 1.3440 support cluster.
